ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP screening against domestic and foreign-recognized politically exposed persons; UN Security Council consolidated list; New Zealand Police designated entities under the Terrorism Suppression Act 2002; New Zealand global terrorist and proliferation financing lists under Sanctions Act 2019; and OFAC SDN list as a secondary institutional-banking benchmark. All UBOs, directors, and shareholders must be screened prior to incorporation; positive hits are escalated to the AML compliance officer and to New Zealand Financial Intelligence Unit as required under the AML/CFT Act. Records must be refreshed at each trigger event and retained for five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office – Companies Register (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Latin alphabetic characters; English and Māori names are automatically acceptable. Chinese characters or non-Latin scripts are not permitted in the registered legal name. A transliterated Latin rendering of the Chinese brand name is permitted, provided it is not misleading and is distinguishable from existing registered names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name is rejected, the applicant may file a written request for administrative review with the Registrar of Companies within 20 working days of the rejection notice, demonstrating compliance with section 20 of the Companies Act 1993 and absence of misleading or objectionable character. If the Registrar maintains the refusal, the applicant may reserve and refile with an amended name or appeal to the High Court of New Zealand under Part 19 of the Companies Act 1993. A valid name reservation must be converted into a full incorporation application within the reservation window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is conditionally permissible for a low-risk administrative holding vehicle, provided that a registered physical office address in New Zealand is maintained, mail forwarding is operational, and corporate records are accessible during ordinary business hours. For a fast-casual food franchise with commercial substance, the entity should also maintain a physical trading premises and local operational management office; a virtual office alone is insufficient to demonstrate substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate: approximately 5% probability of an unannounced statutory inspection within the first 12 months for a non-banking, low-risk food franchise entity; probability increases to 15% if an AML threshold trigger, tax anomaly, or commercial licensing complaint arises.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), ss 10 (mode of incorporation), 12 (requirements for registration), 13 (no minimum paid-up capital), 20 (company name requirements), 117-118 (allotment and consideration for shares), 124 (registered office), 151-152 (disqualification and capacity of directors), 188 (meetings of directors), 190 (notice of registered office), 191 (change of registered office); Companies (Incorporation and Registration) Regulations 1993; Financial Reporting Act 2013; Goods and Services Tax Act 1985; Tax Administration Act 1994.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, an autonomous Crown entity operated by the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), discharging the Registrar of Companies function through the New Zealand Companies Register (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic 'Application for Registration of a Company' (Form NZCN/CO/01) filed through the online Companies Register portal, accompanied by the optional Company Constitution (if adopted), Consent to Act forms executed by every first director, an address for service, the registered office physical address (never a post office box), and the statement of share subscriptions/allotment.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital exists under the Companies Act 1993 (s 13). One or more shares must be allotted to at least one shareholder, but the payment of share consideration may be deferred or unpaid. There is no legal escrow account, deposit, or capital verification requirement imposed by the Companies Office; however, if a New Zealand bank is appointed as the merchant acquiring bank for the franchise, banking practice will require deposited trust capital to be evidenced by a subscription schedule.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTIONS PASSED AT THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [●] LIMITED (NZ COMPANY NO. ●) HELD ON [DATE] BY UNANIMOUS APPROVAL, PURSUANT TO SECTION 188 OF THE COMPANIES ACT 1993

1. SHARE SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT: RESOLVED that the share subscription applications of the persons recorded in the share register be approved and that the directors allot the shares set out in the application for registration at the consideration stated therein; the allotment shall take effect immediately upon the issue of the certificate of incorporation, in accordance with sections 117 and 118 of the Companies Act 1993.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE AND ADDRESS FOR SERVICE: RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be established at [Physical Street Address], [City], New Zealand, being a physical address in New Zealand open to the public and not a post office box, and that the Registrar of Companies be notified of the office address and any address for service in accordance with section 190 of the Companies Act 1993.

3. APPOINTMENT OF DIRECTORS AND OFFICERS: RESOLVED that [Name] be and is hereby appointed Chairman of the Board; [Name] be and is hereby appointed Managing Director; and [Name] be and is hereby appointed Company Secretary and Chief Financial Officer. Each appointee has executed a Consent to Act as Director/Secretary, confirms capacity under section 151, and acknowledges the statutory duties set out in sections 131-138 of the Companies Act 1993.

4. CONSTITUTION AND GOVERNANCE: RESOLVED that the Company adopt the Constitution tabled at this meeting with effect from incorporation, or, if no separate constitution is registered, that the default rules contained in Schedule 1 of the Companies Act 1993 shall govern the Company; the Board adopts a delegation matrix for management of the franchise operation.

5. BANKING AND TAX AUTHORISATION: RESOLVED that the Managing Director be and is hereby authorised to open a corporate bank account with a registered New Zealand bank, to apply for the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN), to register the Company with the Inland Revenue for an IRD number, and to file an election for Goods and Services Tax (GST) registration with effect from the commencement of taxable supplies, in compliance with the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 and the Tax Administration Act 1994.

6. MASTER FRANCHISE LICENCE: RESOLVED that the Company be and is hereby authorised to execute the Master Licence Agreement with the franchisor of the 'Chinese Malatang Self-Serve Broth Bowl' system, to receive royalty and licence fee payments by wire transfer as an approved payment rail, and to operate the fast-casual self-serve restaurant under ISIC 5610 / NAICS 722513; this authority is subject to and effective only after the Company is registered under the Food Act 2014 and obtains the necessary territorial authority building, fire safety, and trade waste approvals.

7. FINANCIAL YEAR AND RECORDS: RESOLVED that the accounting records of the Company be kept at the registered office, that the financial year end be fixed as 31 March, and that an auditor be appointed only where the size thresholds of the Financial Reporting Act 2013 require an audit.

ALL RESOLUTIONS WERE PASSED UNANIMOUSLY AND ARE RECORDED IN THE MINUTES OF THE FIRST BOARD MEETING.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Search and Franchise Trademark Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office - public 'Check company names' engine on the Companies Register (register.companiesoffice.govt.nz) and the Intellectual Property Office of New Zealand (IPONZ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a full register search to confirm that the proposed corporate name (including 'Malatang' branding) is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing company, reserved name, or registered trademark of a third party in New Zealand. Where the name is available, reserve it online for a maximum of 20 working days or incorporate immediately with the same name, which effectuates statutory reservation. Verification of the Chinese-character trading name and the Latin-alphabet brand name should be performed against IPONZ's trademark database (Trade Marks Act 2002) to protect the franchise mark.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name in Latin alphabet
Chinese trading name (optional) for the Ma La Tang brand
IPONZ trademark search report or franchise registration certificate
Identity documents of the applicant/franchisor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a direction under section 23 of the Companies Act 1993 that the name is misleading or likely to deceive, file an alternative name using the same portal; alternatively, apply under section 25 for a change of name passed by board resolution before the direction is finalised.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of the Application for Registration and Payment of the Statutory Filing Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office - online Company Registration portal (part of the Whole-of-Government Business Registration Platform)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Application for Registration of a Company (Form NZCN/CO/01) electronically. Provide the proposed company name, the Constitution (if custom provisions are sought), every first director's full legal name, date of birth, residential address and consent to act; the registered office physical address and an address for service (email acceptable if disclosed); and the full names and share allocations of all initial shareholders. Sign the application by the applicant or an agent authorised by resolution; pay the prescribed fee by credit card or direct bank debit. The portal simultaneously collects data for the NZBN and enables optional IRD number registration.
required_dossiers: Completed Application for Registration of a Company (Form NZCN/CO/01)
Company Constitution (optional, executed by the founders)
Consent to Act as Director executed by each first director
Notice of registered office physical address in New Zealand
Statement of share subscription and proposed allotment
Authority of the incorporating agent (if used)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the application, cure any deficiency (address, director consent, or shareholder details) through the Companies Register correspondence function within 10 working days; if the application is rejected and refunded, re-file a corrected application and pay the fee anew. New Zealand does not provide standing appeal rights; judicial review by the High Court is the ultimate remedy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of Certificate of Incorporation and New Zealand Business Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Companies Register) on behalf of the Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval of the application, the Companies Office automatically creates the company, issues the Certificate of Incorporation and allotts the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN). Download the Certificate of Incorporation, the Extract of the Companies Register, and the NZBN certificate from the portal; verify the company name, company number, date of incorporation, registered office, directors, and share allotment.
required_dossiers: Approved Application for Registration
Companies Register Extract
Certificate of Incorporation
NZBN Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any entered detail is incorrect, apply to the Registrar for rectification of the register under section 161 of the Companies Act 1993 (or the general correction function of the Companies Register) by submitting a signed statement and supporting evidence; the Register will be retroactively corrected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue Registration, IRD Number, and GST Election
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) via the Whole-of-Government Business Registration portal (businessregistration.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the consolidated IRD company registration application (IRD 201) and elect to register for GST. GST registration under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 is compulsory once taxable supplies exceed NZD 60,000 per 12-month period; for a fast-casual restaurant, election from the projected opening date is prudent. Register the company for employer obligations (PAYE, KiwiSaver) if staff will be hired; provide the franchise agreement and a projected revenue schedule to facilitate categorisation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
NZBN Certificate
Company Constitution
Director personal identification and IRD numbers
Franchise master licence agreement
Projected revenue and GST registration request
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD requests further details of the corporate structure (for non-resident shareholders), file Forms IRD 332/333 (Non-Resident Withholding Tax schedules) and a director/shareholder declaration within 20 working days; if the IRD assigns an incorrect GST effective date, apply for a correction through myIR or by service call to the Business Integrity team.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening and AML/CFT Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered New Zealand commercial bank (ASB, ANZ, BNZ, Westpac, or a licensed non-bank deposit taker) corporate client onboarding desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a complete application for a corporate business account with dual payment rails: (i) local point-of-sale (POS) merchant account and (ii) inbound SWIFT/wire receipts for franchise royalties. Provide the bank's AML/CFT officer (under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009) with the company constitution, certificate of incorporation, extract, director passport copies, and the ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) declaration demonstrating the underlying family/trust ownership structure. The bank will classify the restaurant as low AML risk and assign a merchant category code (MCC) for 5812 eating places.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
NZBN Certificate and Companies Register Extract
Company Constitution
Board resolution opening the account and appointing signatories
Passport copies and residential address proof of every director
Ultimate beneficial ownership declaration and trust deed (if applicable)
Executed franchise agreement and projected cash flow statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries non-resident directors or trust ownership, provide a statutory declaration by a New Zealand lawyer or chartered accountant certifying the corporate structure and source of funds; if the application is declined, escalate to the bank's specialised 'Fintech/Franchise' unit or approach a second-tier licensed bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Food Act 2014 Registration - Food Control Plan Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry for Primary Industries - New Zealand Food Safety (NZFSA) in conjunction with the Territorial Authority (City or District Council Environmental Health Unit)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because the business involves immediate cooking and self-service of broth bowls to consumers, it ranks as a higher-risk food service activity requiring a Food Control Plan (FCP) under the Food Act 2014. Complete the MyFCP template or engage a registered food safety verifier to draft the plan. Submit the FCP through MPI's verifier process and register the business with the territorial authority; display the registration certificate at the shop premise; implement environmental health inspection upon opening.
required_dossiers: Completed Food Control Plan (MyFCP or custom)
Floor plan and equipment schedule of the Malatang self-serve station
Temperature control and cleaning log templates
Waste cooking oil collection agreement
Ventilation/extraction system specification
Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MPI or the verifier issues a non-compliance notice, amend the corrective actions and resubmit for verification within 5 working days; if a food safety improvement notice is issued, submit a compliance report to the verifying agency. If registration is refused, appeal to the District Court under section 45 of the Food Act 2014.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Building Consent, Fire Safety, and Occupational Clearance for the Restaurant Fit-Out
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Territorial Authority (Building Consent Authority - BCA) and Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ), together with WorkSafe New Zealand enforcement under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before fitting out the self-serve broth bowl premises, obtain building consent from the territorial authority under the Building Act 2004 for internal fit-out, structural load of floors (broth island and water tank), ventilation, and cooking equipment installation. Fire safety requires compliance with the New Zealand Building Code Fire Safety clauses (C/AS2), an evacuation scheme approved by FENZ where the premises hold more than 50 occupants, and annual building warrant of fitness (BWOF) for fire alarm and emergency lighting. Electrical and plumbing certificates must be issued by licensed tradespeople certified by the Electrical Workers Registration Board (EWRB) and the Plumbers, Gasfitters and Drainlayers Board. Register the workplace with WorkSafe only if hazardous substances are stored; otherwise maintain a health and safety hazard register covering broth burn risks, slips, and steam exposure.
required_dossiers: Building Consent application (form and architectural drawings)
Structural load calculations and geotechnical report (B1/B2 compliance)
Fire hazard analysis and FENZ evacuation scheme application
Building Warrant of Fitness schedule (post-completion)
Electrical Certificate of Compliance (EWRB) and plumbing certificate
Trade waste discharge consent to the local council
Health and Safety at Work hazard register and staff induction record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BCA requests further engineering information, respond with revised calculations within the 10-day statutory notice period; if the building consent lapses, apply for an extension under section 49 of the Building Act 2004; for FENZ refusals, seek reconsideration under section 75 of the Fire and Emergency Act 2017 or appeal to the District Court.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry for Primary Industries - New Zealand Food Safety (NZFSA) jointly with the Territorial Authority (City or District Council Environmental Health unit); co-regulator: New Zealand Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) for nationally significant matters and the Regional Council for discharge consents under the Resource Management Act 1991.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Business Registration Certificate (Food Control Plan) under the Food Act 2014; Territorial Authority 'Eating Place / Fast-Casual Self-Service Restaurant (ISIC 5610 / NAICS 722513)' trade premises licence; Building Code Compliance Certificate and annual Building Warrant of Fitness at the physical premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: New Zealand Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) for national-level considerations; operative local regulator: Regional Council / Unitary Authority under the Resource Management Act 1991 and its National Environmental Standards for Air Quality (NES-AQ)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - No formal Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) required. An ISIC 5610 restaurant fit-out and broth-cooking operation does not meet the mandatory EIA threshold under Schedule 4 of the Resource Management Act 1991. A discretionary resource consent is required only for discharge to air/water or noise if the premises are non-compliant with the relevant district plan; routine trade waste discharges to the municipal sewer are authorised by council bylaw rather than a regional consent.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater (trade waste): discharge to licensed council sewer under the Trade Waste Bylaw - typical geometric limits: pH 6.0-10.0, temperature at point of discharge < 60°C, total suspended solids (TSS) < 600 mg/L, fats/oils/grease (FOG) < 300 mg/L, and no prohibited substances; a grease interceptor with monthly maintenance log is mandatory. Air emissions: cooking steam and particulate must be extracted through a certified canopy duct; discharge must not create a 'noxious or offensive effect' under section 17 of the Resource Management Act 1991 - oil condenser filters or carbon filters are prescribed where the extract outlet is adjacent to residential units. Noise: boundary limits per NZS 6802:2008 (typically 50 dB LAeq day / 40 dB LAeq night for mixed-use zones) unless a district plan relaxation applies. Solid waste: separated recycling of cardboard/plastic and contracted collection of waste cooking oil under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 and the council Waste Management Bylaw.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Inland Revenue / Te Tari Taake Inland Revenue), Wellington, New Zealand; online portal: myIR (secure Inland Revenue digital services portal)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity obtains a statutory IRD number by applying through the Inland Revenue myIR portal or by submitting Form IR742 (Application for an IRD Number for a Non-Resident). The applicant must provide certified Certificate of Incorporation, entity constitutional documents, registered office and principal place of business, directors and ultimate beneficial ownership particulars, and confirmation of any New Zealand fixed establishment. If the entity undertakes a taxable activity in New Zealand or supplies remote services to New Zealand resident consumers, it must register for GST through myIR using Form IR402 or the online GST registration service; registration is compulsory once the NZD 60,000 rolling 12-month taxable supply threshold is exceeded or, for non-resident suppliers of remote services, before supplies are made where that threshold is likely to be exceeded. The IRD number serves as the New Zealand TIN and the GST registration number is the GST ID.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone - Non-resident International Company not carrying on a New Zealand taxable activity and deriving no New Zealand-sourced income; such entity is outside the ordinary New Zealand resident corporate income tax base. Any New Zealand-sourced income or business carried on through a fixed establishment in New Zealand remains taxable, and the entity may be required to register as a non-resident GST supplier for imported remote services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No United States-style check-the-box election is available in New Zealand. New Zealand adopts hybrid mismatch rules under subpart FH of the Income Tax Act 2007 to neutralise tax avoidance through hybrid entities and instruments. A non-resident supplier may elect to register voluntarily for GST under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 even if below the compulsory threshold, subject to Inland Revenue approval and ongoing GST compliance obligations.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 (NZ$60,000) in any 12-month rolling period for taxable supplies made in the course of a New Zealand taxable activity; non-resident suppliers of remote services to New Zealand consumers are registrable when their total supplies to New Zealand residents exceed NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand operates a Peppol-based e-Invoicing framework via the NZ e-Invoicing network; e-invoicing is voluntary, not mandated by law. There is no real-time fiscal clearance obligation, no government-approved digital stamping regime, and no mandatory tax authority API pre-validation for invoices. GST returns are filed electronically through myIR and use-of-money interest and shortfall penalties apply for non-compliance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods are zero-rated where the supplier exports the goods to a place outside New Zealand before or within the statutory timeframe, generally within 28 days of supply, and retains appropriate commercial and customs evidence. Supplies of services are zero-rated when provided to a non-resident outside New Zealand and the supply does not relate to New Zealand land or goods physically present in New Zealand at the time of supply; certain international transport and related services also qualify. The supplier must hold proof of export, non-resident status of the recipient, and evidence that the consideration is received from offshore.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window export declaration)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill issued by the carrier
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank repatriation/FX receipt advice evidencing settlement from the offshore buyer
Commercial Invoice and export sales contract confirming the zero-rated supply
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may audit export zero-rating claims using customs data matching, bank remittance analysis, and commercial records. If goods are not physically exported within the statutory period or services are not genuinely supplied to a non-resident, the supply is re-characterised as taxable at 15% GST and the entire refund amount is clawed back, with use-of-money interest accruing from the original refund date. Shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 range from 20% for an unacceptable tax position, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion; criminal prosecution may also follow for knowingly false GST returns or fraudulent claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) is the central bank, monetary authority, and prudential regulator of the systemically important payment and settlement infrastructure. New Zealand does not maintain a classic foreign-exchange control administration; the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989, the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, and the Overseas Investment Act 2005, administered through the Overseas Investment Office, set the limited regulatory perimeter. Payment clearing rails are supervised by the Reserve Bank through the Payments NZ owned settlement systems, including the Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS), and FX derivative market conduct is regulated by the Financial Markets Authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is freely convertible on both the current account and the capital account. New Zealand maintains no exchange-control approval, no centralised rationing of foreign currency, no restriction on opening and maintaining foreign-currency bank accounts, and no exchange ticket or liquidation system for trade proceeds. Profit, royalty, dividend, interest, and loan-capital remittances to non-residents are contractual matters rather than administrative FX licensing matters. Practical hurdles are limited to: (i) the transacting bank's due diligence under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009; (ii) New Zealand tax clearance, in particular non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) at the relevant statutory rate under the Income Tax Act 2007 for dividends, interest, and royalties, the Approved Issuer Levy option for qualifying interest, and, where the International Company is tax-exempt in its home territory, the need for a letter of exemption or tax-residence certificate to support any claim for treaty benefits; (iii) the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's external statistical reporting for external financial claims and liabilities of NZD 1 million or more; and (iv) screening under the Overseas Investment Act 2005 only if the transaction will acquire sensitive land or significant business assets within the statutory thresholds. No foreign-exchange surrender or purchase-fixing requirement applies to any NZD transaction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. New Zealand has imposed no export-proceeds surrender obligation, no minimum repatriation timeline, and no mandatory conversion ratio since the dismantling of exchange controls in 1984. The CK_IC licensor may hold export and royalty proceeds in any currency, convert at freely negotiated rates, and allocate funds between the New Zealand domestic pool and offshore multi-currency accounts without central-bank approval. The only residual requirements are: (a) anti-money-laundering cash declarations and reporting for the physical import or export of currency or bearer negotiable instruments equal to or above NZD 10,000 under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 and associated regulations; (b) bank-level transaction monitoring and prescribed transaction reporting; and (c) Reserve Bank of New Zealand balance-of-payments and external-position statistical returns where aggregate external claims or liabilities equal or exceed NZD 1 million. None of these imposes conversion, retention, or surrender constraints on export receipts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies), Ministry of Business, Innovation, and Employment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 20 working days after the annual return date, being the anniversary of incorporation or the approved alternative date set by the Registrar.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An overdue annual return triggers a Registrar compliance notice; continued non-filing may lead to removal (strike-off) from the Companies Register after formal notice. Directors may also be liable for default penalties of up to NZD 10,000 under the Companies Act 1993.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Financial Statements and Independent Auditor's Report if the audit mandate is triggered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies (for FMC reporting entities); retained by the company for non-reporting private companies; Inland Revenue for tax coverage.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: If compulsory, financial statements and the auditor's report must be finalised within five months after balance date or within the period required by the applicable enactment; otherwise records are aligned to the annual tax balance date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare, audit, or retain required financial statements where mandated is an offence under the Companies Act 1993 and the Financial Reporting Act 2013, with fines up to NZD 10,000 plus continuing daily penalties; directors may be disqualified for persistence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Food Business Registration and Annual Verification Confirmation under the Food Act 2014
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local territorial authority and the Ministry for Primary Industries recognised verifier (Food Control Plan / National Programme).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Registration must remain current; annual verifier confirmation must be completed before the expiry date stated in the latest verifier certificate. Changes to operator, premises, or food activity must be notified within 10 working days.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating without current registration or verification is an offence under the Food Act 2014; penalties include infringement fines up to NZD 5,000, court fines up to NZD 50,000, and immediate prohibition of trading or closure of the premises.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies where the company is an FMC reporting entity under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (e.g., listed issuer, licensed bank, insurer, non-bank deposit taker, or manager of a managed investment scheme), or where its constitution or a valid shareholders' resolution requires audit. A small non-reporting private company is otherwise exempt from statutory audit unless shareholders holding at least 5% of voting shares requisition an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand GAAP as issued by the External Reporting Board; for-profit entities apply NZ IFRS (Tier 1), NZ IFRS with Reduced Disclosure Regime (Tier 2), or the XRB Simple Format Reporting standard for eligible small owner-managed companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A standard non-reporting private company has no standalone annual UBO filing to the Registrar. The annual return must confirm current directors, shareholders, and shareholdings. Any share issue or transfer must be recorded in the share register and notified to the Companies Office through the prescribed change filing at the time of the transaction. The statutory registers are reconciled at the annual return date, and supporting transfer instruments are retained for at least seven years.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Interests Register (director and shareholder interests, where maintained)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 450 – USD 1,500 per annum for a standard registered office service or local agent retainer.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – USD 8,000 per annum for a small to medium private company statutory audit; USD 1,500 – USD 3,500 for a review engagement if audit is not mandatory.
